history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 559 (Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga, id 'mahakaleshwar-jyotirlinga-ujjain-madhya-pradesh') - this CSV row describes the same temple. One of the twelve Jyotirlingas and one of the most sacred Shiva temples in India, situated near the Rudra Sagar lake in Ujjain. The lingam is believed swayambhu (self-manifested) and dakshinamurti (facing south) - unique among Jyotirlingas. Legend (per MP Tourism): King Chandrasena's devotion and the boy Shrikhar's prayers led Shiva to manifest as Mahakal and slay the demon Dushanana, after which he stayed as the Jyotirlinga; the Varaha Purana places the site at the nabhi (navel/centre) of the earth. The temple suffered in medieval invasions and was grandly reconstructed 1734-1739 by Ramchandra Baba Shenvi, a general of Ranoji Scindia, in Maratha style. The complex is three-storied: Mahakaleshwar at ground level (sanctum below ground), Omkareshwar above, and Nagchandreshwar on the third storey. Famous for the daily Bhasma Aarti (4-6 AM) in which the lingam is smeared with sacred ash.

name: Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga Temple
town_description: Ujjain, on the banks of the Kshipra River, is one of the seven sacred cities (Sapta Puri) of Hinduism and hosts the Simhastha Kumbh Mela every 12 years. It is an ancient centre of astronomy and Shaivism, home to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga and a rich cluster of temples including Kal Bhairav, Harsiddhi, and Mangalnath.
